headline: Majors overbought with RSI extremes while whales rotate ETH to cold storage and stablecoins flow onto exchanges.
paragraphs: The regime is unambiguous: all seven majors trade above their 200-day simple moving average, and MACD sits above signal across the board. Bitcoin dominance sits at 59 percent. That much is a bull-market skeleton. But the momentum picture is deeply compressed. Bitcoin's RSI reads 82, Ethereum 79.5, SOL 85.7, and XRP 80.6. Those numbers live in overbought territory, the space where momentum has run hard and has little runway left before it needs to rest. MACD is above signal, yes, but an RSI in the 80s on a daily chart means buyers have pressed their advantage to the limit. Volatility remains elevated: Bitcoin 30-day realized volatility is 43.5 percent, Ethereum 70 percent, SOL 50.5 percent, and XRP 81.5 percent. The crowd is in greed (73 on the Fear and Greed Index, with a 30-day range of 25 to 73), and the last seven days show aggressive moves higher: Bitcoin up 25 percent, Ethereum up 31.85 percent, SOL up 29.77 percent, and XRP up 48.25 percent. All four of those are off their 12-month highs by large margins (BTC 36.8 percent, ETH 48.1 percent, SOL 60.5 percent, XRP 52.6 percent), which tells you the rally has recovered from a deeper draw but has not reclaimed the year's peak.

On the derivatives side, funding rates tell a coherent story: Bitcoin charges 0.78 basis points per 8 hours (8.6 percent annualized), and the rest of the majors are heavier. Ethereum funds at 1 basis point per 8 hours (11 percent annualized), SOL at 1 basis point (11 percent), and XRP at 1 basis point (11 percent). Those annualized rates are not extreme, but they are not cheap: they say longs are paying to hold their positions. Open interest is substantial (Bitcoin 2.3 billion USD, Ethereum 1.47 billion, SOL 279 million, XRP 110 million), and the positioning is tilted long. Bitcoin's long-to-short ratio stands at 1.0, meaning equal feet on both sides, but Ethereum sits at 1.2 longs per short, SOL at 1.85, XRP at 2.14, and DOGE at 3.5. The further you go down that list, the more skewed toward longs. Liquidations in the last 10 to 24 hours show more longs being flushed than shorts across the board: on Bitcoin, 7 million USD in longs versus 5.5 million in shorts; on Ethereum, 10.7 million longs versus 4.96 million shorts; on SOL, 4.94 million longs versus 2.14 million shorts. That is the tape of a market that has run and is now testing the patience of overleveraged bulls.

Whale moves and stablecoin positioning offer a crucial counterweight to the bullish setup. Over the last 24 hours, 110.8 million USD in crypto moved off exchanges net, but the composition is telling: Ethereum saw 146 million USD leave exchanges (out of Binance), while Bitcoin saw 35.2 million USD move onto exchanges (into OKX). More pressingly, when you look at the weekly net whale flows, the picture has flipped. Week ending August 3 saw 1.128 billion USD move off exchanges. But the three weeks since then have seen consistent inflows: 544 million on to exchanges in the week ending August 10, 102 million in the week ending August 17, and 834 million in the week ending August 24. That is an accumulation of roughly 1.48 billion USD moving onto exchanges over the last three weeks, a material reversal from the prior week's outflow. Stablecoin float remains flat (308.6 billion USD, up just 0.01 percent over 30 days), but 236.6 million USD in stablecoin buying power is sitting idle. Large stablecoin transfers moved onto Binance (137 million USDC, 100 million USDT), the margin venue where much of this leverage lives.

The tension is clear: price has stretched higher while positioning has grown more crowded and more tilted long, funding has climbed to modest but real cost, and whales have shifted from consistent outflow to consistent inflow over the last three weeks. RSI extremes and a rapid seven-day rally do not guarantee a pullback, but they do mean the market has priced in its optimism and is trading on thin air. One asset, ADA, already trades below its 200-day line (the only major to do so), which is a faint signal of sectoral weakness. The two-directional pressure on Bitcoin (whales selling into the rally) and on Ethereum (whales pulling coins to cold storage in size) deserves careful watching. A retest of the 50-day moving average, a flip in funding from positive to negative, or a reversal in the weekly whale inflow pattern would all signal that this compression is beginning to release.
